main_text.l: Rem a Natura(nam & hoc Phi-losophum decebat) mutuatus fum: Non enim eadem mihi Virtutes Cardinales recenfentur, quae vulgo: vulgo hae Prudentia, Justitia, Fortitudo, Temperantia; mihi iste Diligentia, Obedientia, Justitia, Humilitas. Prudentia manifefte excidit (viderunt id ante me complures) hac fructus Virtutis & administraculum, a non Virtus: Convenit inter nos de Justitia: Ambigitur ergo tantum de Fortitudine & Temperantia. Sed hae abeffe pofunt a Virtutis exercitio, forte non fimul, fed faltem fingulae: nam inter adverfa, nullus eft locus Temperantiae: b inter fecunda,
{a} Lumen clariffime illi praelucens in via, qua exit in officium.
{b} Quippe quae imperiofae voluptatis jugum dunta-xat & dominium excutit.

page.notes: Marks a and b are reference marks in the text, keyed to the two notes below. The first line of the page is set in larger italic type and the phrase "Rem a Natura(nam" is printed as shown. Some words in the text are doubtful due to the scan, notably "Temperantiæ", "fingulæ" and "dunta-xat"; the spelling "Virtutes" and "Prudentia" as printed.
